one_line: Paramara king of Malwa (c. 1010–1055 CE), overseeing routes, villages, and administrators from his court at Dhara and Ujjain.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, medium-tall, athletic but scholarly build
appearance.face: oval face with warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes under slightly arched brows, short neatly trimmed moustache, a small tilak on the forehead, default expression calm and observant with a slight analytical intensity
appearance.hair: thick black hair parted slightly off-center, gathered into a smooth mid-length knot at the back of the head (small low bun) wrapped with a narrow maroon cloth band, with a simple gold circlet resting low on the forehead
appearance.costume: era-appropriate royal attire of Malwa: a full-sleeved, knee-length cotton angarakha in deep ivory with fine maroon edging and subtle block-printed floral butis, tied to the right side with visible cords; over it a rich maroon silk uttariya draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back like a shawl; a finely pleated off-white waistcloth/dhoti wrapped to the ankles with a narrow maroon border, worn over tight-fitting ivory churidar-style leg wraps for modesty; dark brown leather sandals; jewellery limited to a thin gold necklace with a small circular pendant, a pair of small gold kundala earrings, and a simple gold armlet on the right upper arm; at his waist a narrow maroon cloth belt supporting a small palm-leaf manuscript case and a ring of tiny bronze seals
appearance.signature: a rolled copper-plate charter tied with a braided cord and sealed with a round copper seal bearing a small incised emblem, held in his left hand like an administrative decree

ref_desc: Bhoja of Dhara is a mid-30s medium-brown Paramara king with an oval face, neat moustache, black hair in a low bun with a maroon band and gold circlet, wearing an ivory angarakha, maroon silk uttariya, off-white ankle dhoti, simple gold jewellery, and holding a rolled copper-plate charter sealed with a round copper seal, in maroon, ivory, warm brown, gold, and off-white tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Bhoja of Dhara: a mid-30s Paramara king of Malwa with an oval face, medium-brown complexion, sharp dark eyes, short trimmed moustache, and a calm, analytical expression. His thick black hair is parted slightly off-center and tied into a smooth mid-length low bun at the back, wrapped with a narrow maroon cloth band, and he wears a simple gold circlet low on his forehead. Dress him in an ivory knee-length full-sleeved angarakha with fine maroon edging and subtle tiny block-printed floral motifs, tied to the right, over tight-fitting ivory leg wraps and an off-white ankle-length dhoti with a narrow maroon border. Drape a rich maroon silk uttariya from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back like a shawl. Add a thin gold necklace with a small round pendant, small gold kundala earrings, and a simple gold armlet on his right upper arm, plus a narrow maroon cloth belt at the waist holding a small palm-leaf manuscript case and a ring of tiny bronze seals. Put dark brown leather sandals on his feet. In his left hand he firmly holds a rolled copper-plate charter tied with cord and sealed with a round copper seal, which is his key prop. Use a palette dominated by maroon, ivory, warm brown, gold, and off-white, and present front, side, and back views to clearly show his consistent face, hair, costume, and the copper-plate charter.
